ai.definition: Optical interconnects are hardware solutions that replace traditional electrical copper traces with silicon photonics for high-speed communication between chips, particularly in data centers.
ai.howItWorks: They utilize laser-driven light modulation to transmit data at terabit speeds, significantly reducing heat generation compared to conventional electrical methods.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the limitations of electrical interconnects such as power consumption and thermal management issues in high-density chip-to-chip communication.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves integrating photonic components onto silicon substrates using advanced semiconductor fabrication techniques.
ai.buildProcess: Components are designed, fabricated, and tested for integration into larger systems before final assembly.
ai.costDrivers: High initial R&D investment, specialized equipment costs, and the need for precise alignment in packaging processes contribute to higher manufacturing costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected growth as demand for high-speed data center interconnects increases, but still requires further standardization and cost reduction.
ai.regulation: Currently not heavily regulated due to the nascent stage of widespread adoption; however, safety standards for laser emissions may apply.
ai.risks: Technological obsolescence, supply chain disruptions, and integration challenges with existing infrastructure are potential risks.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability in niche markets but faces competition from established technologies requiring cost reduction strategies.
ai.futureDevelopment: Ongoing research focuses on improving efficiency, reducing costs, and expanding application areas beyond data centers to other domains like AI and HPC.

glossary.def: The science of light and its applications in information processing, communication, and energy.
The process of creating semiconductor devices by layering various materials on a substrate using precise techniques.

subsystems.name: Photonic integrated circuit (PIC)
subsystems.role: routes and manipulates light on a silicon chip.

subsystems.name: Light source
subsystems.role: provides the continuous-wave laser light that the data is written onto.
parts: external laser module (1310 nm or 1550 nm)

subsystems.name: Modulator
subsystems.role: converts a fast electrical data signal into an optical one.

subsystems.name: Photodetector and receiver
subsystems.role: turns incoming light back into an electrical signal.

subsystems.name: Fiber coupling and packaging
subsystems.role: gets light reliably in and out of the chip.

subsystems.name: Module or co-package
subsystems.role: houses the optics with the switching or compute chip.
parts: or co-packaged optics on a substrate

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the PIC wafer
buildSteps.detail: Waveguides are patterned on 300 mm silicon-on-insulator wafers using deep-ultraviolet lithography, the same toolset as advanced CMOS.

buildSteps.title: Form modulators and detectors
buildSteps.detail: Ion implantation creates the diode structures for modulators; germanium is grown selectively and patterned into photodetectors.

buildSteps.title: Add metal and vias
buildSteps.detail: Copper wiring connects the photonic devices to the electronic driver and amplifier chips.

buildSteps.title: Attach the laser
buildSteps.detail: A III-V laser die is either bonded to the PIC or kept in a separate module and coupled in with lensed fiber.

buildSteps.title: Couple the fiber
buildSteps.detail: Fiber array units are actively aligned to on-chip couplers and fixed in place, a step that dominates assembly cost.

buildSteps.title: Test and burn-in
buildSteps.detail: Every optical channel is tested for bit-error rate and power before packaging.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the module or co-package
buildSteps.detail: The PIC is placed in a pluggable transceiver or bonded directly alongside a switch ASIC on a common substrate.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and link
buildSteps.detail: Modules are plugged into switches or accelerators, and the optical link is trained and monitored in the data centre.

prerequisites.why: photonic chips are made on established CMOS lines, giving low cost and high volume.
they must switch light hundreds of billions of times per second with low loss.
misalignment of a fraction of a micrometre loses most of the light.
putting optics on the same package as the switch chip is demonstrated but only beginning to ship.
multi-vendor interoperability lets data centres mix equipment from different suppliers.

pathway.milestone: pluggable 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers in data centres
pathway.unlocks: high-bandwidth links between switches and between racks with lower power than copper.
removes the electrical loss of long copper traces from the switch faceplate to the chip.

pathway.milestone: optical I/O chiplets for GPUs and accelerators
pathway.unlocks: chip-to-chip and board-to-board links at terabit speeds with less heat.

pathway.milestone: all-optical switching fabrics inside AI clusters
pathway.unlocks: scaling to many thousands of accelerators without an electrical bottleneck.
